summary: The Apify SDK is the official Node.js SDK for building Actors on the Apify cloud platform. It is not a standalone crawling library — it is a lifecycle wrapper around Crawlee (the actual crawler engine, pulled in as a dependency) and the Apify REST API client. The SDK provides Actor lifecycle management (init/main/exit), persistent storage abstraction (datasets, key-value stores, request queues), proxy configuration, platform event handling (aborting/migrating signals), and pay-per-event (PPE) budget charging. Verified from source code: the crawl logic itself is deferred entirely to @crawlee/core — this SDK cleanly separates platform orchestration (storage, events, proxy, charging) from crawling mechanics. It also includes a patched ApifyClient that intercepts pushData calls for transparent PPE charging via AsyncLocalStorage, a clever design pattern for automatic billing without user code changes.

maturityAssessment.claimedMaturity: The README makes no explicit 'production-ready' claim but markets the SDK as the official, supported way to build Apify Actors, backed by a commercial cloud platform. The existence of migration guides (v3), CI badges, and a mature release workflow (51 releases) strongly implies production-grade expectations.

maturityAssessment.contradictionFlags: Minor: The README describes the SDK as 'The scalable web crawling and scraping library' but the actual crawling engine (Crawlee) was split out into a separate @crawlee/core package. The README itself acknowledges this — 'you can also install the crawlee module, as it now provides the crawlers that were previously exported by Apify SDK' — so this is documented, but a casual reader might expect crawling logic within this package. In reality this is infrastructure/glue code, not a crawler. No other flags; the maturity signals are strong.

findings.description: 1. Actor lifecycle management (init, main user function wrapper, graceful exit with configurable timeouts) with automatic cleanup of event listeners and storage teardown. 2. Platform event management — websocket-based connection to Apify platform events (ABORTING, MIGRATING, PERSIST_STATE) with automatic graceful shutdown and reboot handlers. 3. Multi-backend persistent storage: Dataset (append-only JSON objects, max 9MB per item), KeyValueStore (records with MIME types, auto-saved state via getAutoSavedValue/useState), RequestQueue (BFS/DFS URL crawl ordering). All support local filesystem or Apify cloud storage backends. 4. Proxy configuration factory (ProxyConfiguration) that integrates with Apify's proxy service with country, session, and group selection. Validates proxy connectivity during init unless opted out. 5. Pay-per-event (PPE) budget management via ChargingManager — calculates remaining budget, enforces cost limits, supports per-event pricing, batches events, and overcharges by one to trigger platform termination when limit is hit. 6. Structured input handling with prefilled defaults from JSON schema (Input Schema), and support for encrypted input secrets via private key cryptography. 7. Actor-to-Actor calls (call/start/callTask) and Actor transformation (metamorph/reboot). 8. Ad-hoc webhook creation for Actor run events. 9. Extends and patches Crawlee's @crawlee/core for platform integration (re-exports Dataset, RequestQueue, KeyValueStore from Crawlee).
findings.evidence: 1. Actor lifecycle management (init, main user function wrapper, graceful exit with configurable timeouts) with automatic cleanup of event listeners and storage teardown. 2. Platform event management

apiSurface: Users interact via the static `Actor` facade: `await Actor.init()` → `const input = await Actor.getInput()` → user logic → `await Actor.exit()`. Storage shortcuts: `Actor.pushData(item)`, `Avatar:setValue(key, value)`, `Actor.getValue(key)`, `Actor.openRequestQueue(name)`. These internally create a singleton Actor instance and delegate to it. For the platform, users call `Actor.call(actorId, input)` or `Actor.callTask(taskId, input)` to invoke other Actors (serverless Jobs-style chaining). `Actor.createProxyConfiguration({groups: ['datacenter'], countryCode: 'US.'})` returns a proxy config object passed directly to a Crawlee crawler constructor. `Actor.useState('myState', defaultCrew)` provides auto-persisted reactive state backed by a KeyValueStore. For PPE, users call `Actor.charge({eventName: 'search', count: 1})` or rely on implicit charging from `Actor.pushData(data, eventName)`. The static API also includes `Actor.getEnv()` for a typed parse with all ~40 Apify environment variables.
integrationPoints: This SDK would serve as the outer orchestration shell for Veridian If deployed on Apify. The actual scraping logic (Playwright browser launches, page resolution, selector queries, HTTP redirects) would live in the user function passed to `Actor.main()` or wrapped around Crawlee ecosystem classes. For a non-Apify pipeline: 1) The storage system could be used locally with a `CRAWLEE_STORAGE_DIR` directory — datasets and key component stores write JSON+text files to disk, providing a file-based data mesh usable by downstream ETL tools. 2) The `openStorage()` module with `forceCloud: true` allows hybrid local/cloud mode where scraped data is pushed to Apify datasets for cloud access while HTML is stored locally. 3) `Request 4) The proxy configuration is independent of the platform (it uses Apify proxies but the credential resolution comes entirely from env vars, making it usable outside Apify). 4) The ChargingManager only works fully on the Apify platform — without `ACTOR_IS_AT_HOME`, it runs in no-op or warning mode. For monetization in standalone Veridian, charging would need to be replaced.
strengthsForVeridian: 1. Clean separation of concerns — the SDK does not mix crawl logic with platform logic, which aligns with Veridian's own design principle of using Playwright directly and not needing a crawler framework. 2. The persistence model (datasets as append-only JSON streams, key-value stores as typed files) is simple, debuggable, and matches an ETL pipeline's need for accumulated data. 3. The ProxyConfiguration logic for Apify proxy selection (auto/manual, groups, country codes) is well-tested and could be used directly if Veridian uses Apify proxies. 4. PPESquirrel management is sophisticated and well-commented — if Veridian needs to eventually become a paid/usage-metered service, the budget calculations and per-event pricing model are reusable patterns. 5. Strong TypeScript typings throughout, making integration safe. 6. The environmental variable-first configuration is good for 12-factor deployment. 7. Minimal lock-in — the SDK does not mandate the Apify platform; many components work locally or in any Docker/VM environment.
weaknessesForVeridian: 1. Zero crawling capability — this SDK contains no HTTP client, no selector engine, no browser automation helpers. The entire value is orchestration. It is useless for Veridian without Crawlee or manual Playwright calls. 2. Platform dependency for key features — `Actor.call()`, rename privileges, metamorph, reboot, and webhooks are Apify-only and will no-op or warn in a standalone pipeline. PPE charging only operates meaningfully on the Apify platform. 3. The singleton pattern and global config state (`Configuration.storage.enterWith(this.config)`, `CoreConfiguration.globalConfig = ...`) creates hidden coupling — if Veridian needs multiple independent scraping pipelines in the same process, the singleton design becomes problematic. 4. The dependency tree is heavy for what this code provides — this is a monorepo glue package pulling in @crawlee/core (which is itself large with the full Crawlee engine), apify-client (HTTP client), plus the helpers. For Veridian's needs (deterministic scraping, not a web crawler queue), this is significant bloat. 5. No retry truncation, no schema validation of input beyond basic `ow` validations, and no built-in concurrency controls — those are in Crawlee. 6. The code is tightly coupled to Apify's env var namespace — running outside Apify means managing ~40 bespoke environment variables with undocumented interdependencies.
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
